subject: Renewal structure options: layered commit + deferred burst
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@crestlinehealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@crestlinehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal options and potential expansion

Hey Connor,

Hope you're well — our existing term with Redwood ends 2027-01-15 and the execs want to lock in capacity for the next cycle. We're evaluating a couple of structures and wanted to understand what you can support from a commercial and operational perspective:

- Prefer a co-term with our other vendor contracts (goal: align to 2028-12-31)
- Open to multi-year (2 or 3 yr) in exchange for price comfort / credits
- We have a predictable spike pattern in Q1 and Q4; interested in a phased ramp with burst capacity on demand (ideally deferred billing or credits)
- Need clarity on auto-renew opt-out windows and termination notice periods

Can you send options and a short commercial summary? Procurement is on copy — they will want a redline-friendly amendment and SOC2 evidence.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Patel
Director of Platform Ops — Crestline Health
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@crestlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal options and potential expansion

Sam — thanks for the clear brief. Short answer: yes, we can support co-terming, multi-year pricing, and a phased ramp with a burst buffer. High-level options attached (Proposed_Amendment_Draft.docx) but below is an executive summary to kick off the conversation.

Option A — 24-month co-term (preferred)
- 12-month base commitment year 1 + agreed ramp in year 2 (50% -> 100% capacity)
- 6% discount on committed spend vs list
- Burst capacity via "shadow credits": 200k token credits that can be consumed and invoiced monthly or converted to committed allocation at quarter boundaries
- Auto-renew: default ON with 60-day opt-out window (we can extend to 90 for procurement)

Option B — 36-month (deep annualization)
- Front-loaded credits (to cover Q1/Q4 spikes), 10% discount on committed spend, 1% annual escalator
- Longer notice for termination (90 days) and additional service SLA commitments

Next steps: if you like Option A, I can run the numbers with Finance and loop Marissa for approval on the discount and Kimberly for legal redline. Can we schedule a 30-min call this week? I attached a usage extract (Crestline_Renewal_Usage_Report_Q3.xlsx).

Cheers,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal options and potential expansion — need pricing + legal guidance

Team — forwarding Crestline's ask. Key asks: co-term to 2028-12-31, 2–3 year term, phased ramp with burst credits, and clarity on auto-renew window. My recommended commercial posture: propose Option A (24-month co-term with shadow credits) and offer a one-time onboarding credit to offset Q1 spike.

Specific asks:
- Marissa: can we approve 6% discount and 200k token shadow credits for the 24-month deal? If procurement pushes for 36-month, what's the minimum discount (floor) Finance will accept?
- Kimberly: please confirm any mandatory legal language for burst credits and whether we can keep auto-renew default but extend opt-out to 90 days. Also need SOC2 link to send back to procurement.
- Karthik: any regional billing implications if we co-term to calendar-year end?

Proposed deal id DL-2026-0789. Attachments: usage extract and amendment draft.

Thanks — Connor

- We're inclined toward a 2-year co-term structure but want a phased ramp: commit 60% year 1, 100% year 2.
- We prefer burst capacity to be invoiced as consumed rather than pre-bought credits; would you support invoiced burst with a capped monthly charge (we'd like predictability)?
- Auto-renew default is acceptable only if the opt-out window is 90 days.
- Procurement asked for the SOC2 report and an initial redline on the amendment. I've attached the procurement contact for DocuSign logistics.

Procurement will review the amendment once you provide the invoice/cap model for burst and the SOC2 link.

Best,
Sam

Attached: Proposed_Amendment_Draft.docx (redline-friendly), Mutual_Action_Plan.pdf (key milestones: pricing sign, legal redline, DocuSign, onboarding kickoff). Also linking SOC2 and the hubspot deal: https://docs.redwood.com/shared/soc2-report and https://hubspot.com/deals/ DL-2026-0789.

- Kimberly: prepare contractual language for invoiced burst cap and extended opt-out.

If all good, I'll create the DocuSign package by Thursday and schedule a short sync to walk through the amendment.
